title: Samoa Bans Single-Use Plastic Bags and Straws
reason: Multiple independent sources confirm Samoa's Waste (Plastic Ban) Management Regulation 2018, endorsed by Cabinet, took effect January 30, 2019, banning import/manufacture/export/sale/distribution of plastic shopping bags, packing bags, and straws, with a SAT $10,000 fine (100 penalty units) for violators. Exemptions exist for food-safety packaging (frozen meat, ice, produce, biscuits, etc.). The ban's timing meant vendors at the 2019 Pacific Games hosted in Samoa could not use single-use plastics, and the Games were subsequently praised by UNEP as the first 'green' Pacific Games. All material details in the event description are corroborated.

verifications.reason: Multiple independent sources confirm all material details: Samoa's Cabinet endorsed the Waste (Plastic Ban) Management Regulation 2018 in 2018, and the ban on single-use plastic shopping bags, packing bags, and straws took effect January 30, 2019. This meant vendors at the 2019 Pacific Games (hosted in Apia, Samoa) could not legally use single-use plastic products - the event was celebrated by UNEP as the first 'plastic free'/green Pacific Games. Non-compliance carries a fine of SAT $10,000 (100 penalty units). Exemptions exist for food-safety packaging (e.g., bags for frozen meat, local produce). All figures, dates, and actors match the event description precisely.
